chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Abd al-Malik ibn Utba, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about something that reaches us from the garments of the Kaaba, whether it is permissible for us to wear any of them. He said: 'It is permissible for children, for the Qurans, and for the pillow, seeking blessing thereby, if God wills.'
ai.seo_question: Can Muslims wear clothes from the Kaaba for blessing?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the permissibility of wearing garments from the Kaaba, specifying that they are suitable for children, used to wrap Mushafs, or employed as pillows to seek barakah. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly view that the sanctity of these textiles extends beyond ritual exclusivity, allowing their use in daily life as vessels of spiritual blessing, provided the intention is reverent. The narration underscores the practical application of sacred objects in fostering piety among the faithful.
